topic:
Making New Friends as an Adult  
Useful expressions: "break the ice," "common interests," "stay in touch."
script: Hey everyone, welcome to "Chillwave B2".
I'm Ethan.
Today, I want to chat about making new friends as an adult.
I bumped into a neighbor at the grocery store last week, and we ended up bonding over obscure board games.
So, grab a drink, relax, and let’s break the ice about how to find common interests and stay in touch without awkwardness.
A few weeks ago, I met a guy named Jake at a board game café downtown.
We started chatting after he asked me what my favorite strategy game was—heh, totally broke the ice with a game question.
Turns out we both loved old-school classics like Catan and Ticket to Ride.
We exchanged numbers and made a point to stay in touch by messaging once a week.
Now we meet up every Friday for a few hours, and he even introduced me to his friends.
How about you—have you ever bonded with someone over a shared hobby?
Last month, I signed up for a weekend pottery class on a whim.
I met a guy named Sam who kept cracking jokes about clay—helped break the ice.
We realized we both loved bad 90s rock bands and terrible puns.
After class, we swapped numbers and agreed to meet at a local coffee shop.
Staying in touch was easy since we’d plan monthly “music and coffee” hangouts.
Have you ever bonded with someone over something totally random like music or coffee?
So whether it’s through games, clay, or something else entirely, those little shared moments can turn into real connections.
Heh, sometimes the best friendships start with a simple “Hey, I love that band too!” or even a joke about bad puns.
Maybe the next time you’re at a café or a store, you’ll find your own common interest waiting just around the corner.
Don’t forget—it’s okay to break the ice with a smile or a question about someone’s favorite album.
And if things click, a quick text or coffee plan can help you stay in touch without the pressure.
Let me know your stories sometime—maybe you’ve got a friendship that started over something totally unexpected.
Another cool thing I’ve noticed is how “hitting it off” can happen anywhere—even at a coffee shop line.
It just means you and someone quickly realize you vibe well together, like when you both laugh at the same joke or finish each other’s sentences.
Heh, I once hit it off with a barista over our mutual hatred of cold brew—totally random but real.
Once you hit it off, keeping in touch feels more natural, like a “low-pressure” friendship where you don’t have to plan big stuff.
So if you ever feel a connection, just say, “Hey, we really hit it off! Let’s grab coffee sometime—no pressure!”
Alright, that’s about all I’ve got for tonight.
Remember, sometimes a small conversation can lead to a big connection.
Thanks for hanging out and listening in—your time means a lot.
Catch you next week, and maybe you’ll have a new friend story to share. Goodnight!
